title: Recommend a model for one role and present the reasoning
intent: The role's core job and its explicit prompt rail: 'Present the reasons, not just the names.' The fixture gives a full recommend_models payload; a weak model reads off the suggested_model field, a strong one uses the reason, the VRAM number, and the alternates to answer the 'why' the operator actually asked.
prompt: What model should the ingestion agent be running on this machine, and why?

source_facts: Machine: 64GB RAM (60GB sizing budget), 16 cores, linux, NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, 16GB VRAM, nvidia runtime available.
Ingestion's current model is openrouter:z-ai/glm-5.2 and the recommendation status is 'switch' to ollama:qwen3:14b.
The stated reason: ingestion is high-volume, latency-tolerant and mostly distillation; qwen3:14b at q4_K_M needs ~9.0GB VRAM and keeps page bodies and transcripts off a metered API.
Alternates offered: ollama:gemma4:e2b (tier-1 fast, local) and openrouter:z-ai/glm-5.2 (tier-3 quality, cloud).
Nothing overcommits: 14.5GB of 16GB VRAM and 21GB of 60GB RAM if every suggestion loaded at once.
The payload's closing note says suggestions can be verified with the test probe in Settings → Inference and that local models must be pulled first — never without asking.
traps: Answering with the model name and nothing else, which is the exact failure the prompt rail was written against.
Inventing a VRAM figure instead of using the ~9.0GB the payload states.
Claiming the switch was made. This agent cannot edit the agents table; it can only recommend.
Skipping the fact that qwen3:14b is not installed yet and would need a pull the operator has to approve.
judge.guidance: Reward an answer that gives the recommendation, the reason in the operator's terms (volume, latency tolerance, cost of sending transcripts to a metered API), the VRAM fit against 16GB, and a next step — pull it, then verify with the probe in Settings → Inference. Reward mentioning an alternate and when it would be the better pick. Penalize any claim of having applied a change.
